players.product: dispensers and laser reflow bonders for semiconductor packaging

quarterly_data.signal: Half-year report (consolidated, K-IFRS): Q2 2026 revenue KRW 77,314,344,467 vs KRW 64,454,895,135 in Q2 2025; Q2 operating profit KRW 23,097,012,503 vs KRW 9,828,238,539; Q2 net income KRW 34,943,233,828. H1 2026 revenue KRW 139,726,171,281 vs KRW 94,858,091,251; H1 gross profit KRW 53,717,897,364; H1 operating profit KRW 38,515,822,441 vs KRW 12,746,563,056; H1 net income KRW 53,920,100,662 (finance income KRW 31,233,590,897 includes gains on listed-share investments). Revenue by entity (KRW thousand): Protec parent (dispensers, die bonders, heat-slug and solder-ball attach, laser bonders, logistics equipment and parts) 96,429,824; Minami (Japan; screen printers, ball placers) 4,229,281; P&M (pneumatic cylinders) 25,546,429; PMT (probe cards) 34,349,696; intercompany elimination -20,917,675. Parent separate basis: H1 revenue KRW 96,429,824,228 vs KRW 74,483,851,921, operating profit KRW 31,394,578,393 vs KRW 15,613,510,310. Consolidated revenue by region (KRW thousand): Korea 84,319,396, China 22,278,651, other 33,128,124; exports 55,406,775. Average selling price of dispensers and die bonders KRW 389 million in H1 vs KRW 336 million in FY2025. FY2025 reference: revenue KRW 230,543 million, operating profit KRW 46,307 million.

Customer concentration (names undisclosed): consolidated H1 2026 revenue from customer A KRW 34,200,395K and customer B KRW 24,869,080K (H1 2025: KRW 56,521,568K and KRW 3,141,753K). On the parent's separate basis, customers A-D contributed KRW 24,660,980K, KRW 11,425,081K, KRW 10,665,602K and KRW 10,491,722K of KRW 96,429,824K revenue (H1 2025: KRW 2,964,349K, KRW 5,188,567K, KRW 705,944K and KRW 3,126,333K). The customer list also names LG Electronics and LG Innotek among domestic buyers. Trade receivables rose to KRW 95,109,339K from KRW 57,921,242K at year-end; USD receivables US$48,597,416.89. Products are built to order with orders typically placed 16 to 24 weeks ahead, so no order backlog is disclosed; customer advances (contract liabilities) were KRW 7,645,130K vs KRW 3,922,455K at year-end and inventory KRW 88,112,242K (work in progress KRW 64,479,157K).

quarterly_data.signal: Products and R&D per the half-year report: Protec lists a laser bonder (2024) that uses a laser heat source from below to bond high-performance chips such as GPU logic dies or HBM onto interposers or PCB substrates, with sales generated; a next-generation laser-assisted bonder (2022) using an in-house large-area laser source and controller in place of imported parts, with sales generated; a Micro Solder Ball Attachment System (2022, Minami) with sales; and a Copper Pin Attachment System (2025, Minami) for high-aspect-ratio copper pins replacing solder balls. It holds a technology-royalty agreement signed 2024-12-21 with an undisclosed overseas company A for sales beyond that counterparty. The report states demand for HBM and 2.5D/3D heterogeneous packaging keeps rising and HBM and related advanced-packaging equipment demand is expected to expand, and that the company is developing bonder and laser-application equipment for future growth. Consolidated R&D spend KRW 7,447,334K = 5.3% of revenue; patents held 318.
quarterly_data.figure: Laser bonder for GPU/HBM onto interposer (sales since 2024); Copper Pin Attachment System (2025); R&D KRW 7,447,334K (5.3%)

quarterly_data.signal: Production and purchasing: Protec does not disclose capacity or utilisation because its tools are custom-built to order and peak volumes use outside contractors; H1 production equals sales at KRW 139,726,171K. Raw-material purchases of KRW 79,229,648K were led by mechanical parts KRW 26,447,046K (33.4%), pneumatic cylinders etc. at subsidiaries KRW 25,581,749K (32.3%), other bonder materials KRW 12,259,634K (15.5%), electrical KRW 5,602,696K (7.1%) and electronics KRW 3,996,294K (5.0%); suppliers are not named. H1 PP&E purchases KRW 5,949,436,666 (construction in progress additions KRW 3,993,645K; balance KRW 8,804,004K); the company states no large new facility investment is in progress.
